= Module: <code>settings.d/</code> =

[https://github.com/Sidiberlin/hdp/blob/main/app/settings.d <code>app/settings.d/</code>] contains numbered PHP
configuration files, auto-loaded in ascending filename order by
[https://github.com/Sidiberlin/hdp/blob/main/app/LocalSettings.BlueSpice.php <code>app/LocalSettings.BlueSpice.php</code>],
which <code>setup.sh</code> appends a <code>require_once</code> for at the end of the generated
<code>LocalSettings.php</code>. This mechanism enables ~130 BlueSpice extensions in a
specific order with their configuration, and is where this fork’s two
critical infrastructure fixes and the ChatBot→<code>chatbot-proxy</code> wiring live.

== Responsibilities ==

* Enable MediaWiki/BlueSpice extensions and skins (<code>wfLoadExtension()</code> / <code>wfLoadSkin()</code>) in dependency order.
* Configure extension-specific settings (<code>$GLOBALS</code> overrides).
* Layer configuration in tiers: core → MWStake → MediaWiki defaults → Free → Pro → Farm → fixes → Discovery skin → GovTech (ChatBot) → ChatBot config.

== Loading Mechanism ==

[https://github.com/Sidiberlin/hdp/blob/main/app/LocalSettings.BlueSpice.php <code>app/LocalSettings.BlueSpice.php</code>]:

<syntaxhighlight lang="php">$settingsDir = "$IP/settings.d";
foreach ( glob( $settingsDir . "/*.php" ) as $conffile ) {
    $searchString = preg_replace( '/\.[^.\s]{3,4}$/', '', $conffile ) . ".local.php";
    if ( file_exists( $searchString ) ) {
        $conffile = $searchString;   // e.g. 100-ChatBot.local.php overrides 100-ChatBot.php
    }
    if ( !in_array( $conffile, $loaded ) ) {
        require_once $conffile;
    }
}</syntaxhighlight>
A <code>NNN-Name.local.php</code> file next to any <code>NNN-Name.php</code> is loaded ''instead''
of the base file — an environment-specific override mechanism, unused by
default in this repo.

== Notable Patterns / Gotchas ==

* '''<code>config_prefix</code> matters.''' <code>app/extensions/ChatBot/extension.json</code> declares no <code>config_prefix</code>, so MediaWiki’s default <code>GlobalVarConfig</code> reads '''<code>wg</code>-prefixed''' globals for this extension’s config (<code>$config-&gt;get('BmbfDeepsetApiChatUrl')</code> reads <code>$GLOBALS['wgBmbfDeepsetApiChatUrl']</code>, not <code>$GLOBALS['BmbfDeepsetApiChatUrl']</code>). <code>100-ChatBot.php</code> sets the <code>wg</code>-prefixed names explicitly, with a comment recording that this was previously a silent no-op bug (unprefixed globals set, extension reading <code>wg</code>-prefixed ones and always getting the <code>extension.json</code> default <code>&quot;&quot;</code>) — see <code>docs/QA-REPORT.md</code> Bug 5. This is exactly the gotcha described in [[chatbot-extension.md#configuration-wg-prefixed-mediawiki-globals|chatbot-extension]].
* '''<code>$wgSQLMode</code> beats the MariaDB server config.''' The Wikimedia dev image’s <code>PlatformSettings.php</code> (required before <code>settings.d/</code> loads) sets <code>$wgSQLMode = 'STRICT_ALL_TABLES,ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY'</code>. Because MediaWiki’s DB layer applies <code>$wgSQLMode</code> on every connection, fixing only the server-side <code>sql_mode</code> (<code>docker/mariadb/sql-mode.cnf</code>) is not enough — <code>050-Fixes.php</code> strips <code>ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY</code> from <code>$wgSQLMode</code> itself, ''after'' <code>PlatformSettings.php</code> has already run, which is the layer that actually wins.
* '''Number prefix is a hard dependency order, not just a display order.''' <code>090-GovTech.php</code> loads <code>ChatBot</code> after <code>030-</code>/<code>040-</code> have already enabled <code>BlueSpiceFoundation</code> and <code>BlueSpiceExtendedSearch</code>, because <code>ChatBot</code>’s <code>extension.json</code> registers into <code>BlueSpiceExtendedSearch</code>’s <code>ExternalIndexRegistry</code> attribute at registration time.
* '''<code>100-ChatBot.php</code> is the newest file (highest number)''', added by this fork specifically to override the four <code>BmbfDeepsetApi*</code> URLs after <code>090-GovTech.php</code> has loaded the extension — config files can safely load after the extension that reads them, since MediaWiki only evaluates <code>$config-&gt;get()</code> at request time, not at extension-registration time.
* '''<code>090-GovTech.php</code> is intentionally tiny''' — 3 lines, just <code>wfLoadExtension('ChatBot')</code>. All actual ChatBot configuration lives in the separate <code>100-ChatBot.php</code>, keeping “load the extension” and “configure it for this deployment” as distinct, independently-overridable files.
